decision.thesis: All cash, the twenty-seventh all-cash row and the sixth decision of ramp week 5. Monday 10-12 is not yet decomposed (the 2026-10-12 feedback page is tomorrow's). The cached closes: Genting 1.88 -> 1.45 (-22.87%) on 90,366,100 shares and Genting Malaysia 1.49 -> 1.23 (-17.45%), the first session after the RM1.25 billion rights-issue reports; the titles say limit down, an IDSS suspension and the largest fall since 1998, and a CIMB estimate of 18% earnings dilution, all google_news titles without terms. ^KLSE +0.59% to 1,618.01 with volume 0 on the bar. The control book, which holds 200 Genting, fell 2.23% to USD 954.23. A post-announcement fall whose terms are still unknown is a claim about the issue price, not the company; Genting's round trip at one lot is now 5.98%. Maybank +1.43%, Tenaga +1.24%; NVIDIA -1.29%, Apple +1.29%, Microsoft +1.14%. Two all-cash claims are graded, both correct against a losing control. Claim: nothing in the fundable universe beats cash over 21 sessions.

evidence.genting_rows: google_news titles 10-12 01:47Z-04:09Z: limit down, IDSS suspension, largest fall since 1998, CIMB 18% dilution; no terms

mistakes: paper-2026-10-08-allcash-21d-7bb6 listed Genting's drift as a reason against it; Genting closed 1.45 on 10-12, the reason held for a cause the page could not have seen.
paper-2026-10-09-allcash-21d-81d7 and paper-2026-10-10-allcash-21d-f51e named Genting's round trip and unknown terms as reasons against it; one lot from Friday's 1.88 would have lost 22.87% on 10-12.
The control's -2.23% on 10-12 is a passive holding through an announced dilution; it is the benchmark the all-cash claims grade against.
lessons: An announced cash call can move a name more in one session than its fitted distribution allows; a sigma fitted on ordinary days says nothing about a day the share count changes.
A passive control that holds the affected name makes every all-cash claim look right that day; read those grades as the control's loss, not a finding about names.
